newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK jobless total down to lowest for six years.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK jobless total down to lowest for six years.

text.p: British unemployment has fallen to its lowest level for more than six years giving a boost to the ruling Conservatives as they struggle in opinion polls ahead of the May 1 election.

Official figures issued on Wednesday indicated the number of people recorded as out of work fell by 41,100 to 1.71 million in March -- the thirteenth successive monthly decline. The unemployment figure was the lowest since September 1990 and gave a jobless rate of 6.1 percent.
The jobs data was the last before the election and was welcomed by Prime Minister John Major's government in its drive to convince electors that "Britain is booming".
But despite a raft of good economic news, the Conservatives are still some 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party in opinion polls.
Other figures announced on Wednesday showed that the underlying yearly change in average earnings in February rose to five percent, compared with 4.75 percent the previous month.

The public finances were looking healthy with a public sector financial deficit of just 22.8 billion pounds ($37.01 billion) for the 1996-97 financial year, below the official forecast of 26.4 billion pounds.
The figures were in line with economists' expectations.
"On balance, a broadly positive set of numbers," said economist Andrew Snowball of the Cooperative Bank.
Other economists said the data meant that Britain was ironically now on course to meet the Maastricht criteria for a single European currency.
But both the Labour and Conservative parties say it is highly unlikely that Britain would want to join a single currency in the first wave.
Labour, out of power for 18 years, said on Wednesday that if it won power it would review how the jobless figures are compiled.
Media reports said the figures currently understate the level of unemployment but Major on Wednesday dismissed the reports as "total and utter rubbish.".
